description:
**Divergence** — numbered draft revision appears in AGENTS.md titles at 4 lines each in 5 files:
- crate-jmap-chat-server/AGENTS.md L28, L34, L157, L174 — `draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00`
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/AGENTS.md L28, L34, L123, L139 — `draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26`
- crate-jmap-tasks-server/AGENTS.md L28, L34, L123, L139 — `draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06`
- crate-jmap-filenode-server/AGENTS.md L28, L34, L122, L138 — `draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13`
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/AGENTS.md L28, L34, L123, L139 — `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01`
- vs crate-jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md — cites only "RFC 8621" (stable, no revision suffix)

**Maintainer cost**: IETF drafts rev every few months. The current revision is hardcoded in 4 places per AGENTS.md across 5 files = 20 call sites. When a new draft revision lands, no automated check catches stale citations. The workspace draft-tracker beads (e.g. `bd:JMAP-v3ff` for the chat-spec edit) update spec content but do not necessarily sweep every AGENTS.md citation. A contributor reading crate-jmap-metadata-server/AGENTS.md today sees `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01` and may think they're tracking the current revision when in fact the IETF could have published draft-02 weeks ago.

**Fix options**:
(a) Switch to unversioned form ("draft-ietf-jmap-metadata") in AGENTS.md citations; track the current revision only in `PLAN.md` and `Cargo.toml`-adjacent README, where a single point of update is feasible. Recommended.
(b) Add a doc-tests-style check to CI that grep-matches AGENTS.md numbered citations against an external source. Higher complexity, lower value.

This is a recurring class of staleness — fix the structure (option a) rather than chase the contents.
title: 5 extension-server AGENTS.md titles pin to numbered draft revision (draft-ietf-jmap-X-NN); canonical mail-server cites stable RFC 8621 with no suffix — citation drift is a staleness hazard
